solution.operation: Bring down next group (70), form new dividend 970

solution.description: Cross-add to find how many whole bases the product contains: take either number and add the other's deviation, 43 plus minus 3 or 47 plus minus 7. Both routes give the same left part, 40.

solution.operation: Multiply the left part by the base
solution.description: This gives the first part of the final product, representing the base multiple.

solution.operation: Compute the right part – product of deviations
solution.description: The product of the deviations contributes the remainder. Since both deviations are negative, their product is positive.
Add the two parts together: 2000 from the base multiple plus 21 from the deviations gives 2021, so 43 times 47 is 2021.

common_mistakes: Treating base 50 like a power of ten and simply writing 21 beside 40; because the base is 50 the left part must actually be multiplied by 50.
Dropping the minus signs when cross-adding, which gives 46 or 50 instead of the correct left part 40.
Making the product of the deviations negative; minus 7 times minus 3 is a positive 21, so it is added, not subtracted.
